justification: Implementing GHG reduction targets can reinforce the development of net-zero technology for road vehicles, as reducing emissions can create demand for low-carbon fuels and technologies.
Reducing GHG emissions can lead to increased food production costs, which may impact food affordability, but this can also create opportunities for sustainable food systems and fair pricing.
Reducing GHG emissions can aid in the reduction of pesticide use, as sustainable agriculture practices are often promoted as a means to achieve both GHG reduction and pesticide reduction targets.
Achieving GHG reduction targets can enable the development of competitive and sustainable agricultural practices, supporting the growth of the agricultural sector.
Reducing GHG emissions can lead to job creation and protection in the renewable energy sector, supporting social security and worker protection.
The implementation of net-zero technology for road vehicles may lead to increased costs for low-carbon fuels, impacting food affordability and potentially constraining agricultural production.

The development of net-zero technology for road vehicles can support the reduction of pesticide use, as electric vehicles can be powered by renewable energy sources, reducing the need for fossil fuels and promoting sustainable agriculture practices.
The growth of the net-zero technology market for road vehicles can create opportunities for sustainable agriculture and support the competitiveness of the agricultural sector.
The expansion of the net-zero technology market for road vehicles can lead to job creation and protection in the automotive sector, supporting social security and worker protection.

Increased food production costs due to sustainable agriculture practices can constrain the reduction of pesticide use, as farmers may prioritize cost-effective pest control methods over sustainable ones.
Higher food production costs can impact the competitiveness of the agricultural sector, potentially constraining its growth and development.

Increased food costs can negatively impact low-income households, potentially affecting social security and worker protection, as workers in the food sector may face reduced purchasing power and job insecurity.
Reducing pesticide use can support the growth of sustainable and competitive agricultural practices, promoting biodiversity and ecosystem services.
The reduction of pesticide use can lead to improved working conditions and protection for agricultural workers, supporting social security and worker protection.

Supporting competitive agriculture can lead to job creation and protection in the agricultural sector, supporting social security and worker protection, as well as promoting sustainable agricultural practices.
